story.i_want: Update the current API implementation to utilize a real SQL database connection with connection string managed by configuration
story.so_that: The application can persist data reliably across application restarts and support production-grade data storage instead of in-memory repositories

acceptance_criteria.criterion: SQL repositories implement the same interfaces as in-memory repositories
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given the API is configured with a SQL database connection, When a transaction is created, Then it is persisted to the SQL database

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Connection string is read from appsettings.json configuration
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given appsettings.json contains a valid connection string, When the application starts, Then it connects to the specified SQL database

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Database context is properly registered in dependency injection
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given the application is configured with DbContext, When repositories are instantiated, Then they receive a valid ApplicationDbContext instance

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Existing API endpoints continue to work with SQL-backed repositories
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given the API endpoints are unchanged, When requests are made to transaction and account endpoints, Then they retrieve/persist data from/to SQL database

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Account and transaction data models are properly mapped to database entities
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given the Account and Transaction domain models exist, When data is persisted to SQL, Then the schema correctly represents the domain model

edge_cases.gherkin: Given the database is unavailable, When the application starts, Then it fails with a meaningful error message

edge_cases.criterion: Connection string is missing or invalid
edge_cases.gherkin: Given appsettings.json has no connection string, When the application starts, Then it fails with a clear error
Given the database exists but tables do not, When the application starts, Then migrations create the required schema

edge_cases.criterion: Concurrent access to database from multiple application instances
edge_cases.gherkin: Given multiple application instances access the same database, When transactions are created, Then data integrity is maintained

edge_cases.criterion: Seed data already exists in database on application restart
edge_cases.gherkin: Given seed data exists in the database, When the application restarts, Then no duplicate accounts are created

steps.description: Configure ApplicationDbContext with Entity Framework Core - Define DbSet<Account> and DbSet<Transaction> properties, configure entity mappings using Fluent API in OnModelCreating
Implement SqlTransactionRepository - Create class implementing ITransactionRepository with GetByAccountIdAsync, GetAllAsync, and CreateAsync using Entity Framework Core LINQ queries
Implement SqlAccountRepository - Create class implementing IAccountRepository with GetByIdAsync, GetAllAsync, and GetBalanceAsync methods
Register SQL repositories in dependency injection - Update Program.cs to register ApplicationDbContext with SQL Server provider and SQL repositories
Update seed data initialization - Modify Program.cs to use SQL repositories for seed data with idempotency checks
Configure environment-specific connection strings - Ensure appsettings.json and appsettings.Development.json contain proper SQL Server connection strings
Implement database migrations - Set up Entity Framework Core migrations to automatically create/update database schema on startup
Verify API endpoints work with SQL-backed repositories - Test GET/POST transactions and GET accounts endpoints with SQL backend

unit_tests.description: Verify ApplicationDbContext entity mappings are configured correctly
Test SqlTransactionRepository LINQ queries with in-memory database
Test SqlAccountRepository balance calculation from transactions
Verify Program.cs reads connection string from appsettings.json

integration_tests.description: Verify ApplicationDbContext connects to SQL database and creates schema
Create transaction via API, verify persisted to SQL database, retrieve via API
Create multiple transactions, verify account balance calculated correctly from SQL
Verify 5 test accounts created in SQL database on startup
Restart application, verify no duplicate accounts created
Verify meaningful error message when database is unavailable

e2e_tests.description: Create account, create transaction, retrieve account with updated balance
Create data, restart application, verify data still exists
Create multiple transactions concurrently, verify all persisted correctly

risks_and_mitigations.risk: Database connection failures in different environments
risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: Validate connection string during startup and provide clear error messages. Use environment-specific appsettings files.
Check if accounts exist before creating seed data. Use account IDs to prevent duplicates.
Wrap repository operations in Entity Framework Core transactions to ensure all-or-nothing semantics
Ensure Entity Framework Core handles concurrent access with proper transaction isolation levels

risks_and_mitigations.risk: Schema mismatch between code and database
risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: Use Entity Framework Core migrations to automatically create schema from entity mappings. Validate schema matches design.
Create appropriate indexes per schema design. Use LINQ query optimization and profiling.
Maintain existing ITransactionRepository and IAccountRepository interfaces. Test API responses match expected schema.
